newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast gasoline, diesel prices rise on fire.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast gasoline, diesel prices rise on fire.

text.p: U.S. West Coast gasoline and diesel prices began rising early Monday on news of a fire at Texaco's 98,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) refinery in Wilmington, Calif., traders said.
Bids for CARB-grade gasoline in Los Angeles rose 0.75 cents from Friday to 63 cents a gallon. Conventional unleaded rose one cent to 59 cents a gallon.
Traders said the damaged unit, a hydrotreater, could cause the refinery to lose at least 20,000 bpd of gasoline output.
"The big market impact will be on gasoline," a trader said.
Traders said ample West Coast supply and a drop in NYMEX prices would curb the rally.
"I would expect it to go up as much as one or two cents on the news, but then retrace back to a half a cent," one trader said.
Jet fuel in Los Angeles rose 1.50 cents a gallon to 68/69 cents a gallon, while low sulphur diesel climbed a cent to 67.50/68.50 a gallon.
Offers for CARB diesel appeared to advance a half cent to 75.50 cents a gallon, but bids remained unchanged, traders said.
